# bugs #2691: Internal error need pointerCode for the address of an element of a nested array of pointers

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2691/
- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-2691.patch](../../patches/bugs-2691.patch), commit [`85acd7789`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/85acd778981c116acf3195413ba68a2cd28d3a0c). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The attached Csmith program takes the address of an element of a three-dimensional array of
pointers, `&l_15[1][1][0]`, and stores through that address. Its function `func_1`, without the
Csmith runtime, compiles on r17158 with six sets of mcs51 options: the small, medium, large, and
huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the small and large models. The defect behind the message is
present there. `&a[i][j]` has the type of `a[i][j]` when `a[i]` is an array of object pointers
and is itself an array element, a struct member, or the target of a pointer.

With `long g; long *arr[2][2]; void *varr[2][2]; void *q;`, these expressions fail on r17158:

- `q = &varr[1][1]; *(void **)q = &g;` stops with `need pointerCode` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` with the
  medium, large, and huge models and with `--model-large --stack-auto`.
- `(&arr[0][0])[1] = &g;` stops with `need pointerCode` with each of the six sets of options.
- `*(&arr[i][0])[j]` stops with an internal error in `src/SDCCicode.c` on mcs51, stm8, and z80.
- `&arr[1][0] + 1` is the address plus the size of a `long` on mcs51, stm8, and z80.

## Cause

`geniCodeAddressOf` in `src/SDCCicode.c` returned every lvalue iTemp of pointer type with its type
unchanged. That is right for the operands that `geniCodeDerefPtr` and `geniCodeStruct` make, whose
type is already a pointer to the object. For an element of an array of object pointers,
`geniCodeArray` makes an operand that has the type of the element and marks it with `aggr2ptr`.
`geniCodeAddressOf` returned these operands unchanged as well.

Arithmetic on such an address was therefore scaled by the size of the object that the element
points to, and `(&a[i][j])[k]` accessed an object of that type. Where pointer types differ in
representation, as on mcs51, the address was also treated as a pointer of the element's kind,
which leads to the internal error.

## Fix

`geniCodeAddressOf` returns the operand with its type unchanged only when `aggr2ptr` is not set.
Otherwise the rest of the function gives the operand the type pointer to element, as it does for
elements of arithmetic types. The change is one condition.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-2691.c` has the loop of the ticket's program with a smaller array,
conversions of such addresses to `void *`, pointer arithmetic, and a pointer difference. Without
the patch, the test does not compile on r17158 for stm8, for z80, and for mcs51 with each of the
six sets of options. With the patch, its 12 assertions pass on these eight targets and on host.

On r17176 with the patch, the regression suite for host, the six sets of mcs51 options, stm8, and
z80 and the diagnostics suite ran without a failure. The other ports were not tested.

## Related

- The entry local 0007 describes reads such as `*a[1][1]` through an element of a nested array of
  pointers in mcs51 data memory. The compiler first stores the pointer through itself. The patch
  does not change that.
- The entry local 0008 describes arithmetic on `&fp[i][j]` for a nested array of function
  pointers, which steps by a row. The patch does not change that, because `geniCodeArray` gives
  those operands the type of the array.
- On stm8 only, a store through a negative constant index such as `(&iarr[i][j])[-1] = 5` was
  emitted as `ldw (0xfffe, x), y` and the check of the element then failed in the simulator, which
  was observed and not analyzed because this report covers mcs51.
